regional_context.context: A small town at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers; 2020 population 269.

selected_places.title: Harpers Ferry station

facts.text: The station is in Harpers Ferry and is served by Amtrak and the MARC Brunswick Line.
It has two side platforms serving two tracks.

particulars.text: The station address is 120 Potomac Street.
The historic station building was rebuilt in 1894.

affordances: a place to wait for, meet, or leave someone using rail
two platform sides can separate people who are both at the station
semantic_lures: train travel as an automatic metaphor for life transition

selected_places.title: Jefferson Rock

facts.text: Jefferson Rock is on the Appalachian Trail in Harpers Ferry.
It overlooks the Shenandoah River just before the river meets the Potomac.

particulars.text: The formation is made of masses of Harpers shale.

affordances: a recognizable intermediate point on a route through town
a place where a carried object can be set down briefly

selected_places.title: Lockwood House (Harpers Ferry)

facts.text: Lockwood House stands on the east side of Camp Hill, high above Harpers Ferry.
The building is at 360 Fillmore Street.

particulars.text: It is a large stone-and-brick residence built in 1848.
It later became the first building of Storer College.

affordances: an upper-town landmark for giving directions
a fixed point from which someone can begin or end an errand
semantic_lures: historic building as a container for memory
elevation as moral or emotional ascent
